runs.content: Tuesday's rotation deep-dives AI & Tech + Technology. No new source material had landed in either domain since the last AI-Tech-focus run (2026-09-15, the Kakashii ingest) — today's clippings-sorter batches were all Finance-domain — so instead of re-covering already-flagged pages, deep-read ai-tech-overview.md, technology/overview.md, and a handful of older, previously-undived AI & Tech source pages for a fresh angle. Found one: ai-tech/source-uptime-ai-efficiency-metrics-2026.md (Uptime Institute, Jan 2026) and finance/investor-letters/source-burry-ap-sbc-tragic-algebra-2026-04-07.md run the identical analytical move in two different domains — an industry converging on a flattering headline metric (AI chips' 4-bit-precision TFLOPS, 16x inflated vs. the 64-bit figure; GAAP/Wall-Street-'adjusted' earnings, a $1.7tn 'earnings illusion' once SBC dilution is properly normalised out) that's meaningless without a stricter, less flattering denominator. Neither page cites the other, and several of Burry's own 'Tragic Tier' SBC-abuse names (Palantir, CrowdStrike, Datadog, Marvell) are AI-infrastructure-adjacent companies the wiki elsewhere takes at face value. Concrete next step: cross-link the two pages' See Also sections. Separately, today's Finance portfolio-management-briefing data-integrity catch-up (unrelated to the focus-domain rotation, but new and concrete) surfaced a check_data_quality.py backlog of 804 non-'ok' rows, 106 of which are real, persistent 7-day yfinance-fetch failures on an EU-ticker cluster outside current holdings — distinct from and more actionable than the already-open 'script hung with zero output' thread from 2026-09-21. Concrete next step: pull the actual ticker list and check whether it's the same LSE/Euronext GLOBAL_QUOTE-vs-TIME_SERIES_DAILY quirk already fixed once for WOSG.L. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-21.

Monday's rotation deep-dives Finance + Crypto. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-20), Crypto had no new material (last refresh was 09-19), but Finance had a 15-clipping clippings-sorter batch today, which supplied both connections. First: finance/short-research/source-morningstar-uk-most-shorted-2026-09-18.md flags Ceres Power (CWR, LSE) at 13.29% net short interest — a UK-listed solid-oxide fuel cell (SOFC) company marketed as a 'clean-energy/data-centre power solution' but hit with sell downgrades and a Grizzly Research bear report questioning partnership profitability, against a widening operating loss. finance/ideas/idea-bloom-energy.md's own Competitive Landscape table lists Plug Power (PEM) and FuelCell Energy (MCFC) as Bloom's competitors but omits Ceres — despite Ceres running Bloom's own core SOFC technology, making it the closer technology peer. More importantly, Ceres is a live market test of exactly the 'barely profitable, priced for perfect execution' Bear Case idea-bloom-energy.md already raises about Bloom itself — short-sellers are actively betting against the same AI-power narrative one ticker over, and neither page (nor ai-tech/model-dc-power-regional-balance-2026-06-25.md, which calls on-site fuel cells an unqualified 'immediate — already happening' winner) cites the others. Second: finance/source-guardian-ai-slowdown-bubble-2026-09-20.md names concrete, dated margin evidence — OpenAI 'repeatedly cutting fees to retain customers,' Anthropic's 'adjusted operating income' positive 'only by excluding many real costs' — for exactly the risk ai-tech/data-token-generation-pricing-gpu-comparison-2026-08-05.md already names once, in the abstract, as 'massive margin compression risk if open-weight models close the quality gap,' but elsewhere frames token deflation mainly as a benign scaling story. Neither page grounds the abstract risk in a named company until today's Guardian piece. Concrete next steps: add a Ceres Power row to idea-bloom-energy.md's Competitive Landscape table cross-linked to the short-interest screen; add the OpenAI/Anthropic margin evidence to the AI & Tech token-pricing page's margin-compression Key Insight.
